title: CGAP Freezing Human Tissue in Isopentane
author: Adam Hunter
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.qz7dx9n
materials: Receive tissue and place on ice.

steps.title: Prepare isopentane cooling bath
steps.instruction: Place the isopentane container on dry ice, add dry‑ice lumps until the bath reaches –70 °C for most organs (–40 °C for striated muscle), and monitor the temperature with a –100 °C thermometer. Prepare one pair of forceps with the tip chilled in dry ice for later handling of the weighing boats.

steps.title: Label and chill Falcon tubes
steps.instruction: Place pre‑labelled 15 ml Falcon tubes on dry ice.

steps.title: Cut tissue into experimental pieces
steps.instruction: Using room‑temperature forceps, transfer the first tissue sample onto a petri dish, then cut it into three chunks: one for bulk RNA, one for spatial transcriptomics, and one for fresh dissociation (if not already taken). Place each chunk into a separate weighing boat.

steps.title: Freeze tissue pieces in isopentane
steps.instruction: With the cold forceps (tip chilled in dry ice), grasp one side of a weighing boat and lower the tissue directly into the isopentane, ensuring it does not float out. Hold the piece submerged for 10–20 seconds (until bubbling stops). Drain as much isopentane from the weighing boat as possible before proceeding to the next piece.

steps.title: Transfer frozen tissue to tubes
steps.instruction: Using the cold forceps, place each frozen tissue piece into its correspondingly labelled 15 ml Falcon tube and keep the tubes on dry ice.

steps.title: Store tubes at –80 °C
steps.instruction: Transfer the labelled Falcon tubes from dry ice into a –80 °C freezer.

steps.title: Evaporate residual isopentane
steps.instruction: Remove the Mr Frosty cryo‑container from the dry ice, leave its lid off in a fume cupboard, and allow any remaining isopentane to evaporate.
